title: Tests hand-seed refcheck_edit, bypassing the entry-creation path entirely
evidence:
+      refcheck_edit: dict.from_list([
+        #(
+          "rc-1",
+          model.RefcheckEdit(
+            call_id: "rc-1",

detail: Both tests pre-populate the edit dict keyed "rc-1" instead of driving the control that opens the trio and creates the entry. A slot-keyed creation handler would reintroduce the exact #611 snap-back while these tests stay green.
recommended_fix: Start each test with an empty refcheck_edit; click the open-correct / open-substitute control and assert the entry is created under reference_call_id before typing.

title: Trio data-testids left slot-keyed while the message key moved to reference_call_id
evidence:
text_input(
-        slot,
+        call.reference_call_id,
         "name",
         copy.refcheck_field_name,
         name,
         "refcheck-edit-name-" <> slot,
detail: Same call sites changed the state key but kept slot-suffixed testids. If two rows ever share a slot (original plus substitute), duplicate DOM testids collide — only the state is id-safe now.
recommended_fix: Suffix testids with call.reference_call_id (or slot plus id) so DOM identifiers are row-unique and consistent with the keyed state.
